To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the $ \mathrm{U}(N) $ instanton partition function with $ \Omega $ -deformation parameters $\epsilon_1=\epsilon_2=\epsilon $ in the limit $\epsilon \rightarrow 0 $ is given by the $ \mathrm {U}(N) \rightarrow \infty $ limit of the Mayer expansion of the $ \mathrm U (N) $ -matrix model with $ \mathrm U(N) $ -invariant potential.
the instanton partition functions in Nekrasov-Shatashvili limit are described by TBA equations.

the instanton partition functions in the Ω-deformed $ \mathcal {N} $ = (4,2) and $ \mathcal N $ = 4 SYM theories can be written as sums of products of the partition functions of free massive spin chains, which can be obtained by the thermodynamic Bethe Ansatz (TBA)-like equations.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a novel approach to the analysis of the instanton contributions to the partition function of supersymmetric gauge theories.
the study of integrability of the quantum field theory of the $ \mathfrak{sl}(2)$ Yang–Mills theory on the two dimensional sphere.
the following questions: (i) What is the physical interpretation of the TBA equations?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the TBA equations for the Nekrasov partition functions are a direct consequence of the Mayer expansion.

the Mayer expansion is a powerful method to study the large- N limit of the partition function of supersymmetric gauge theories and, in the case of $ \mathcal {N} $ = (2, 2) supersymmetric theories in two dimensions, to derive the TBA equations.

the TBA equations for the $ \mathfrak{s}\mathfrak{u}\mathfrak{\left(}n\right) $ Toda chain, as well as the corresponding equations for other integrable systems, are the result of a cluster expansion for the partition function of a certain $ \mathcal{\mathcal{N}}=2 $ quiver gauge theory.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have found that the Mayer-cluster expansion of the instanton partition functions in the Ω-deformed gauge theories is a very powerful tool to derive the TBA equations.
we have found an explicit realization of the thermodynamic Bethe-ansatz equations for a class of integrable systems, in terms of gauge theory partition functions.
we have provided a direct derivation of TBA like equations in the context of gauge theory.
The main takeaway from our work is that
in the context of gauge theory the TBA equations are nothing else than the result of the iterated Mayer cluster expansion.
the instanton partition function can be viewed as a generating function of the TBA like equations.
the Mayer-cluster expansion provides a natural and powerful tool to derive TBA equations in the context of gauge theory.
